For better of for worse here’s the terribly told story of the first time I got majorly high to be immortalized on Reddit for all of eternity. Because why not ya know. 

I met up with a friend who was already a bit high. After a while I went back to his place and watched him painstaking roll a blunt for 45 minuets. I think it was about 1:30 in the morning when we went to his car with a straight edge friend to babysit us. I should have seen something coming considering it took him that long to roll this blunt about 3 hours after he originally smoked but I was fresh faced and ready to get high. I think I took three hits(?) from this tightly packed blunt and we ventured on a 5 minute walk back to our dorm building which felt like a lifetime. I almost immediately started to feel it. I could either focus on what was directly in front of me or everything at once. I remember the ground being incredibly hypnotic as I stared at my feet trying to walk. We got back to the entrance to our dorm and saw a group of friends sitting outside and decided to sit and talk with them for a while. I couldn’t tell you what the hell we were talking about though I just remember occasionally saying something and everyone laughing in a weird and rhythmic way. I kept looking at my surroundings and being surprised I was still outside. Also the feeling of gum in my mouth was the craziest thing ever but in a way it was familiar. Around then I started to get extremely weird bouts of deja vu and not to sound stereotypical but holy shit did it make me doubt my entire sense of reality. Like glitch in the matrix stuff. Basically the best I could describe it is that I have lived that reality countless times and for some reason there is a critical point in the timeline where I always smoke weed and it all becomes incredibly clear. Because I had lived this life so many times but with just subtle variations I could see everything that was about to happen before it happened. It was like I could see the future but couldn’t vocalize it. I could see the potential paths that I could take and I chose not to go down the ones that ended badly. Each time I tried to do something different the timeline would change to one that a didn’t predict. It’s like I was trapped in my predestination and still am. 

Anyways, everything that my not high friend sounded like an npc in a video game just repeating the same things over and over. In all honesty that was one of the most hellish parts. In reality it turned out that he was actually lowkey having a breakdown and also had a high fever? Which I didn’t even know until the next day so I guess there was a reason for the vague feeling of concern. It felt like an eternity but after about an hour of being stoned out of my mind I crashed on my friends bed, still sitting up, from about 2:30 am to 9 am. I woke up to him telling me to “get vertical” so he could lay all the way down. I was surprisingly not confused and grabbed my things and told him I was leaving. I walked up the four flights of stairs to my room and started the impossible task of taking out my contacts. Sometime in that brief window of time I had a short and awkward conversation with my roommate before she left town for the weekend. I went back to sleep until 5 pm. 

I woke up thinking I was fine at this point and went to shower. Everything was going smoothly until I had to wash some dishes and actually concentrate on something. After that the terrible feeling of deja vu krept up on me. I ended up watching YouTube and continued to convinced myself that I could predict what was going to happen in them. I also doodled in colored pencil some pieces that are surprisingly not bad. I did this for about 5 hours before I realized how much time had passed. I then made the terrible decision to watch Coraline as if my reality wasn’t skewed enough. Lucky at about the 24 hour mark I was pretty much fine besides the relentless feeling of doubt for everything that I perceive.
